key_insight: The paper reformulates strain gradient elasticity as a first-order mixed system and solves it with a hybridized staggered DG method that is stable and robust for all parameter regimes.
engineering_relevance: It provides a practical finite element framework for high-order solid mechanics problems that avoids boundary-layer issues and remains accurate across small length-scale and nearly incompressible settings.
method: Introduce displacement plus total stress, Cauchy stress, and hyperstress as auxiliary variables.
Discretize displacement/total stress with staggered DG spaces and the two scaled stresses with Raviart--Thomas pairs.
Use hybridization and static condensation so only two skeleton multipliers remain globally coupled.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical inf-sup stability, a discrete Korn inequality, optimal convergence, and numerical experiments confirming parameter-robust rates.
watch_item: The formulation is more complex than standard displacement-based FEM and requires careful implementation of symmetry, mixed spaces, and skeleton coupling.
paper_title: A Hybridized Staggered Discontinuous Galerkin--Mixed Finite Element Method for Strain Gradient Elasticity
